links.outcome: Time to correct diagnostic pathway for patients with initial false suspicion, with vs without iAorta
links.effect: Prospective comparative study (n = 13,846): iAorta shortened time to correct diagnostic pathway from an average of 219.7 (115-325) min to 61.6 (43-89) min.
links.quote: In the prospective comparative study (n = 13,846), iAorta demonstrated the capability to significantly shorten the time to correct diagnostic pathway for patients with initial false suspicion from an average of 219.7 (115-325) min to 61.6 (43-89) min.

links.outcome: Performance across noncontrast CT protocols/sites in real-world study
links.effect: In the real-world study (n = 137,525), iAorta had sensitivity 0.913-0.942 and specificity 0.991-0.993 across various noncontrast CT protocols.
links.quote: In the large-scale real-world study (n = 137,525), iAorta demonstrated consistently high performance across various noncontrast CT protocols, achieving a sensitivity of 0.913-0.942 and a specificity of 0.991-0.993.

links.outcome: Performance and time to diagnosis in prospective pilot deployment in emergency department
links.effect: iAorta correctly identified 21 of 22 AAS patients among 15,584 consecutive chest pain patients; average time to diagnosis was 102.1 (75-133) min.
links.quote: Furthermore, for the prospective pilot deployment that we conducted, iAorta correctly identified 21 out of 22 patients with AAS among 15,584 consecutive patients presenting with acute chest pain and under noncontrast CT protocol in the emergency department.

screen.reason: The study evaluates an AI warning system (iAorta) for detecting acute aortic syndrome from noncontrast CT, including a prospective clinical pilot deployment in the emergency department measuring impact on time to diagnosis.
